State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Davinder Singh vs Make My Trip India Pvt. Ltd. on 2 May, 2017
FIRST ADDITIONAL BENCH

STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, PUNJAB
 SECTOR 37-A, DAKSHIN MARG, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.897 of 2015

 Date of Institution: 12.08.2015
 Order Reserved on: 28.04.2017
 Date of Decision : 02.05.2017

 Davinder Singh S/o Sh. Harbans Singh, aged 40, R/o House No.444,
 Phase-4, S.A.S. Nagar, Mohali, 2nd address New Diamond Jewellers
 Shop No.46-47, Phase 4, Sector 59, SAS Market, S.A.S. Nagar,
 Mohali.
 .....Appellant/complainant
 Versus

 1. Make My Trip India Pvt. Ltd., 243 SP Infocity, Udyog Vihar
 Phase I, Gurgaon, Haryana through its Managing Director,
 having its Local office at Chandigarh i.e. Make My Trip India
 Pvt. Ltd. SCO No.43-44, Level I, Madhya Marg, Sector 8-C,
 Chandigarh through its Manager.
 2. Dipika Chemjong, Senior Executive-Outbound Operations,
 Make My Trip.com, 243 SP Infocity, Udyog Vihar Phase I,
 Gurgaon, Haryana.
 3. Alok Kumar Pandey, Executive, MakeMyTrip.com, 243 SP
 Infocity, Udyog Vihar Phase I, Gurgaon, Haryana.
 .....Respondent/opposite party
 First Appeal against order dated
 15.06.2015 passed by the District
 Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,
 S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali).
 Quorum:-
 Shri J. S. Klar, Presiding Judicial Member
Smt. Surinder Pal Kaur, Member

 Present:-
For the appellant : Sh. Baljinder Singh, Advocate
 For the respondents : Sh. Naveen Sharma, Advocate
 ............................................

 J.S KLAR, PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER :-
The appellant has directed this appeal against order

 dated 15.06.2015 of District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum

 S.A.S. Nagar (Mohali) (in short the 'District Forum), vide which, the
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 2
complaint of the complainant was allowed by directing OPs to refund

50% of the deposited amount of Rs.1,00,000/- alongwith interest

@9% per annum from the dates of deposit till realization; and to pay

lump sum compensation of Rs.20,000/- toward mental harassment

and costs of litigation. The appellant of this appeal is the complainant

in the original complaint before the District Forum and respondents

of this appeal are opposite parties therein and they be referred as

such hereinafter for the sake of convenience.
2. Complainant Davinder Singh filed complaint U/s 12 of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
(in short, "the Act") against the OPs

on the averments that OP no.1 is duly registered under the
Companies Act
1956 having its registered office and it has been

dealing in the business of arranging domestic as well as foreign trips

through online modes. OP nos.2 and 3 are the

representatives/executive officers of OP no.1. OPs gave an

advertisement on television, internet, newspaper etc. with regard to

the assured foreign as well as domestic trips for the tourist, who

wanted to spend their holidays in their desirous countries and cities.

An email was sent to the complainant on 08.03.2014 by the

representative of OP no.1 with regard to holiday package namely

Swiss Delight for five nights and six days for travel during the months

of June, July, August, September, 2014. The total price of the

package was Rs.69,990/- + EUR 459 X 80, as per the prevailing rate

of Euro = INR 106990-INR 17000+INR 3.09% = 92,500/-. The

complainant felt satisfied with the travel package and he deposited

the sum of Rs.60,000/- in the account of OPs. Email was sent to
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 3
complainant after receipt of money by OP no.1 admitting the receipt

of this amount of Rs.60,000/-. The OPs mentioned in the email that

they had booked the tour package of the complainant on booking ID

no.IN1403B6S054485 for departure date i.e. 13.08.2014 from New

Delhi for two adults. The complainant was asked to courier the

documents at the address of OP no.1 and they were sent by the

complainant. OP sent email dated 18.07.2015 asking complainant to

deposit a sum of Rs.50,000/- in the account of OP no.1. The

complainant enquired about the status of his visa from OP no.2. OP

no.2 asked the complainant to deposit Rs.40,000/- to proceed with

the visa file, otherwise the booking would be cancelled. The

complainant deposited this amount in the account of OP no.1

through his credit card on 21.07.2014. The interview for tourist visa

was fixed on 24.07.2014 and OP no.3 was appointed to guide the

complainant with regard to his interview before the Swiss Embassy.

The complainant visited Swiss Embassy on 24.07.2014 for interview.

The complainant was unable to answer the questions in embassy

about the name of hotel booked by the complainant and tickets. The

complainant had to face that problem due to non-disclosure of name

of hotel as well as air tickets to be arranged by the OPs to him. The

visa of the complainant was rejected by concerned embassy, vide

email dated 28.07.2014. The complainant sent email on 28.07.2014

asking OPs to refund the total deposited amount i.e. Rs.1,00,000/-.

The complainant alleged act of OPs as deficiency in service and

unfair trade practice. The complainant prayed for refund of
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 4
Rs.1,00,000/- with interest @18% per annum and any other relief in

his favour, which may be deemed fit by Forum.
3. Upon notice, OPs appeared and filed written reply and

contested the complaint of the complainant vehemently. It was

averred in preliminary objections that complaint is not maintainable

both on merits or as per law. The District Forum has no jurisdiction to

entertain the complaint, as per terms and conditions of user

agreement executed between the parties. It was further averred that

the International Trip and issuance or rejection of visa is the absolute

prerogative of the concerned Embassy only. OPs acted as a

facilitator and they had no role in this regard. OPs firstly

arranged/booked the air tickets and hotel accommodation for the

complainant and his wife and thereafter processed the visa

application annexing therewith details of flights and hotels before

concerned Embassy. Concerned Embassy called the complainant

for interview and his visa was rejected on the ground of

misrepresentation projected by him before the Visa Issuance

Authority. It was further averred that complainant concealed the fact

that on two earlier occasions, his visa for UK was revoked after

issuance and Visa of complainants' wife was also rejected. OPs

denied entitlement of complainant for refund, as per cancellation

policy. OPs controverted the averments of the complainant and they

prayed for dismissal of the complaint by denying any deficiency in

service on their part.
4. The complainant tendered in evidence affidavits Ex.CW-

1/1 and Ex.CW-1/2 alongwith copies of documents Ex.C-1 to C-15
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 5
and closed the evidence. As against OPs tendered in evidence

affidavit of Deepak Taneja, Deputy Manager as Ex.OP-1/1 and

closed the evidence. On conclusion of evidence and arguments, the

District Forum allowed the complaint of the complainant. Dissatisfied

with the above order, the complainant now appellant has preferred

this appeal for enhancement of compensation amount and litigation

costs and for refund the total amount of Rs.1 lakhs alongwith

interest.
5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties at

considerable length and have also examined the record of the case.

The District Forum has already accepted the complaint of the

complainant by directing OPs to refund 50% of the deposited amount

of Rs.1,00,000/- alongwith interest @9% per annum from the dates

of deposit till realization; and to pay lump sum compensation amount

of Rs.20,000/- toward mental harassment and costs of litigation. The

complainant wants enhancement in the amount of compensation in

this case. The order under challenge in this appeal has not been

assailed by the OPs now respondents of this appeal by filing a cross

appeal. The other findings, as recorded by the District Forum

remained unassailable in this appeal before us and need not to be

touched again. We are primarily concerned with this fact as to

whether the complainant now appellant is entitled to enhancement in

the amount of compensation in this case or not. Arguments of

counsel for the appellant and respondents of this appeal heard at

length by us. The counsel for the appellant argued that as per the

directions of OPs, he deposited sum of Rs.60,000/- in their account
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 6
for continuing with the tour package namely Swiss Paris Delight.

OPs sent email to him about receipt of the amount of Rs.60,000/-.

OPs also sent email having booked tour package of complainant on

booking ID no.IN1403B6S054485 for departure date 13.08.2014

from New Delhi for two adults, vide C-2. The OPs further asked the

complainant to courier the documents at the address of OP no.1.

The grievance of the appellant is that in interview, consular put the

questions to him in the Embassy about the name of booked hotel

and details of air tickets, but he could not give the correct answers,

because OPs have not disclosure about them to him. He further

stated that due to non-disclosure of this fact, he faced this problem

which led to rejection of his visa. On the other hand, OPs

controverted this contention of counsel for the appellant on the

record. The counsel for the appellant submitted that OPs outrightly

refused to refund the entire amount to the complainant stating that

the air tickets have already been issued, therefore, the amount

cannot be refunded. The counsel for the appellant further submitted

that the entire stand of OPs that the air tickets and hotel have been

booked is false and frivolous one.
6. We have also examined the record of the case and

perused the order of the District Forum under challenge in this

appeal.
7. The complainant has not traveled on the scheduled dates

and in the absence of any specific provision regarding refund in the

agreement, the OPs are not justified in withholding the entire amount

of Rs.1,00,000/- without providing any such service. The
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 7
complainant applied for Swiss Paris Delight tour package for five

nights and six days for travel during the months of June, July,

August, and September 2014. The OPs did some service to the

complainant and are entitled for retention of some portion of the

deposited amount. Undoubtedly, the visa of the complainant was

rejected, as complainant could not give the proper answers to the

consular of the concerned Embassy. The counsel for the appellant

referred to law laid down in "
Bhupender Singh Ghangas Vs. Make

My Trip Pvt. Limited
" in first appeal no.22 of 2013, instituted on

26.07.2013 and decided on 30.09.2013 by State Consumer

Disputes Redressal Commission, U.T. Chandigarh before us. We

have examined the law cited before us, which was also considered

by the District Forum in its judgment. The agreement executed

between the parties is Annexure B on the record. We find that

complainant suffered rejection of his visa partly on account non-

disclosure of some particulars. This is a case of contributory

negligence in our opinion. The complainant should have been also

cautious in extracting information from OPs regarding the name of

the hotel booked or particulars of the air tickets. The OPs are also

deficient in service in not informing the complainant in this regard.

We, thus, conclude that the District Forum correctly passed the order

directing OPs to refund 50% of the deposited amount of

Rs.1,00,000/- alongwith interest @9% per annum from the dates of

deposit till realization; and to pay lump sum compensation of

Rs.20,000/- toward mental harassment and costs of litigation. We

find no unreasonableness and unfairness in the order of the District
First Appeal No. 897 of 2015 8
Forum. The order of the District Forum is quite equitable within the

parameters of law. We find no illegality in the order of the District

Forum even on the point of quantum of compensation. The

complainant is not entitled to refund of the whole amount deposited

by him with OPs because complainant himself is negligent to some

extent in not extracting the information from OPs before appearing in

Embassy concerned. We affirm the order of the District Forum under

challenge in this case and find not ground to enhance the amount of

compensation.
8. As a result of our above discussions, we find no merit in

the appeal and the same is hereby dismissed by affirming the above

order of the District Forum.
9. Arguments in this appeal were heard on 28.04.2017 and

the order was reserved. Certified copies of the order be

communicated to the parties as per rules.
10. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory

period due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(J. S. KLAR)
 PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 (SURINDER PAL KAUR)
 MEMBER

May 02, 2017
MM
